newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stock exchange says reviewing computer glitch.
newsitem.headline: HK stock exchange says reviewing computer glitch.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said on Thursday it was conducting a review of a "technical defect" in its closing price file after screens erroneously showed a four percent drop in the blue-chip Hang Seng Index.
The exchange said in a statement that the defect in the computer-generated file caused the previous closing prices shown on its system's stock pages to be inaccurate.

The problem was remedied by manually inputting the correct previous closing prices into the corresponding stock pages of the Automatic Order Matching and Execution System (AMS) and the market opened as normal, it said.
The incident had no effect on AMS and the Traded Options system, it said.
The exchange said it informed the Hong Kong Futures Exchange, Securities and Futures Commission and HSI Services Ltd as well as members and traders before the market opened.
The Hang Seng Index, calculated by HSI Services Ltd using data from the exchange, erroneously appeared to fall more than 500 points in the opening minutes of trade on Thursday.
The exchange later said the index fell 228.71 points at its lowest point. It ended the day down 136.32 points at 13,053.28 on profit-taking. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441
